passage: Note from Francis, church volunteer, Christmas Eve. During the carols Samir stood on his toes to see the crib, his mouth open at the candles. He sang the parts he knew, a beat late and loud, and hummed the rest. When the lights dimmed for the last hymn he stopped fidgeting and held his grandmother's hand tightly. Afterwards he asked me whether the star had really moved, and whether the animals had been cold. I said the stories say they were warm. He seemed satisfied, then told me, "I like it when everybody sings together." I did not explain more; he was taking it in his own way. I will invite him to help hang the star next year.

qa.q: What did Samir ask Francis afterwards?
qa.a: He asked whether the star had really moved, and whether the animals had been cold.

qa.q: What was Samir feeling during the last hymn, and what shows it?
qa.a: He felt awe and belonging; he stopped fidgeting, held his grandmother's hand tightly, and said he likes it when everybody sings together.

qa.q: How could Francis support Samir's wonder as he grows?
qa.a: Francis could let Samir take part, like hanging the star, keep answering Samir's questions simply, and welcome harder questions later.

qa.q: How might Samir's grandmother feel watching him?
qa.a: She was probably moved and happy to see him join in, since he held her hand tightly.

grounding: A child feels devotion, wonder and belonging at a festival service through songs, candles and stories.
